content: The use of GLP-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) is recommended to help patients achieve personalized glycemic targets while also providing cardiovascular benefits. Nonsteroidal mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists (MRAs) should be utilized in cases where albuminuria, defined as an albumin-to-creatinine ratio (ACR) of ≥30 mg/g, persists despite normal potassium levels. Calcium channel blockers and diuretics are prescribed to provide additional control of blood pressure when needed. Antiplatelet agents are advised for patients with atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease (ASCVD) to reduce the risk of subsequent cardiovascular events. For lipid management, PCSK9 inhibitors or ezetimibe are recommended in patients who fail to achieve their LDL cholesterol targets with statin therapy alone.
